inductive TmS : Type
  | lit  : Int -> TmS
  | tvar : Nat -> TmS
  | add  : TmS -> TmS -> TmS

def evalTmS (env : Nat -> Int) : TmS -> Int
  | TmS.lit n   => n
  | TmS.tvar k  => env k
  | TmS.add a b => evalTmS env a + evalTmS env b

inductive StS : Type
  | svar   : Nat -> StS
  | sicc   : TmS -> TmS -> StS
  | sinter : StS -> StS -> StS

def memS (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) (x : Int) : StS -> Bool
  | StS.svar s     => senv s x
  | StS.sicc lo hi => decide (evalTmS env lo <= x) && decide (x <= evalTmS env hi)
  | StS.sinter a b => memS senv env x a && memS senv env x b

inductive PdS : Type
  | pmem    : TmS -> StS -> PdS
  | peq     : TmS -> TmS -> PdS
  | psub    : StS -> StS -> PdS
  | pseteq  : StS -> StS -> PdS

def denoteS (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) : PdS -> Prop
  | PdS.pmem e s     => memS senv env (evalTmS env e) s = true
  | PdS.peq  a b     => evalTmS env a = evalTmS env b
  | PdS.psub a b     => forall x : Int,
      memS senv env x a = true -> memS senv env x b = true
  | PdS.pseteq a b   => forall x : Int,
      memS senv env x a = memS senv env x b

theorem memS_svar (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) (x : Int)
    (s : Nat) :
    memS senv env x (StS.svar s) = senv s x := rfl

theorem memS_sicc (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) (x : Int)
    (lo hi : TmS) :
    memS senv env x (StS.sicc lo hi)
      = (decide (evalTmS env lo <= x) && decide (x <= evalTmS env hi)) := rfl

theorem memS_sinter (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) (x : Int)
    (a b : StS) :
    memS senv env x (StS.sinter a b)
      = (memS senv env x a && memS senv env x b) := rfl

theorem denoteS_pmem (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (e : TmS) (s : StS) :
    denoteS senv env (PdS.pmem e s)
      = (memS senv env (evalTmS env e) s = true) := rfl

theorem denoteS_psub (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (a b : StS) :
    denoteS senv env (PdS.psub a b)
      = (forall x : Int, memS senv env x a = true -> memS senv env x b = true) :=
  rfl

theorem denoteS_pseteq (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (a b : StS) :
    denoteS senv env (PdS.pseteq a b)
      = (forall x : Int, memS senv env x a = memS senv env x b) := rfl

theorem boolS_ext {p q : Bool} (h1 : p = true -> q = true)
    (h2 : q = true -> p = true) : p = q := by
  cases p <;> cases q
  . rfl
  . exact h2 rfl
  . exact (h1 rfl).symm
  . rfl

theorem pseteq_iff_mutual_psub (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (a b : StS) :
    denoteS senv env (PdS.pseteq a b)
      <-> (denoteS senv env (PdS.psub a b) /\ denoteS senv env (PdS.psub b a)) := by
  constructor
  . intro h
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    . intro x hx
      rw [← h x]
      exact hx
    . intro x hx
      rw [h x]
      exact hx
  . intro h x
    exact boolS_ext (h.1 x) (h.2 x)

theorem psub_sinter_left (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (a b : StS) : denoteS senv env (PdS.psub (StS.sinter a b) a) := by
  intro x hx
  rw [memS_sinter] at hx
  cases h : memS senv env x a with
  | true  => rfl
  | false => rw [h] at hx; simp at hx

/-
ROUND 3 -- the one requirement r2 left unmet: a free set variable is not
only a PREDICATE-layer atom, it is a BINDER, and the certified pipeline
decides a binder by SWEEPING its box-relativized domain.  r2 proved the
atom layer.  This round builds the binder layer, proves its sweep sound,
and then MEASURES the sweep's domain -- which is where the row's price
actually lives.
-/

/-- The decidable core of `denoteS`, box-relativized.  `psub` and `pseteq`
quantify over all of Int, so the sweep relativizes them to the box exactly
as the pipeline's box layer relativizes an ordinary binder. -/
def checkPdS (box : List Int) (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) :
    PdS -> Bool
  | PdS.pmem e s => memS senv env (evalTmS env e) s
  | PdS.peq a b => decide (evalTmS env a = evalTmS env b)
  | PdS.psub a b =>
      box.all (fun x => (!memS senv env x a) || memS senv env x b)
  | PdS.pseteq a b =>
      box.all (fun x => decide (memS senv env x a = memS senv env x b))

/-- The box-relativized denotation the sweep is actually sound for. -/
def denotePdBoxS (box : List Int) (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool)
    (env : Nat -> Int) : PdS -> Prop
  | PdS.pmem e s => memS senv env (evalTmS env e) s = true
  | PdS.peq a b => evalTmS env a = evalTmS env b
  | PdS.psub a b => forall x, x ∈ box ->
      memS senv env x a = true -> memS senv env x b = true
  | PdS.pseteq a b => forall x, x ∈ box ->
      memS senv env x a = memS senv env x b

theorem checkPdS_sound (box : List Int) (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool)
    (env : Nat -> Int) :
    (p : PdS) -> checkPdS box senv env p = true -> denotePdBoxS box senv env p
  -- `show` first: the target is only DEFINITIONALLY the equation, and
  -- instance search will not unfold `denotePdBoxS` to find the Decidable
  -- instance (the committed slice records the same hazard on
  -- `checkStmtBox_sound`).
  | PdS.pmem _ _, h => h
  | PdS.peq a b, h => by
      show evalTmS env a = evalTmS env b
      exact of_decide_eq_true h
  | PdS.psub a b, h => by
      simp only [checkPdS, List.all_eq_true] at h
      intro x hx hxa
      have hb := h x hx
      rw [hxa] at hb
      simpa using hb
  | PdS.pseteq _ _, h => by
      simp only [checkPdS, List.all_eq_true] at h
      intro x hx
      exact of_decide_eq_true (h x hx)

/-- The statement layer with BOTH binder kinds.  `sallS` binds an ordinary
Int variable; `ssallS` binds a SET -- the constructor the row's lead
subject (`09_Sets#definition-003`, an intersection of two sets the source
gives no comprehension for) needs TWICE. -/
inductive StmtS : Type
  | base : PdS -> StmtS
  | sallS : Nat -> StmtS -> StmtS
  | ssallS : Nat -> StmtS -> StmtS

def updEnvS (env : Nat -> Int) (k : Nat) (v : Int) : Nat -> Int :=
  fun i => if i = k then v else env i

def updSenvS (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (k : Nat) (u : Int -> Bool) :
    Nat -> Int -> Bool :=
  fun i => if i = k then u else senv i

/-- Box-relativized statement semantics.  The Int binder ranges over `box`;
the SET binder ranges over `sbox` -- the list of set assignments the sweep
enumerates.  Soundness below is relative to exactly that list, which is the
whole point: the theorem is easy, the LIST is not. -/
def denoteStmtBoxS (box : List Int) (sbox : List (Int -> Bool))
    (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) : StmtS -> Prop
  | StmtS.base p => denotePdBoxS box senv env p
  | StmtS.sallS k s =>
      forall v, v ∈ box -> denoteStmtBoxS box sbox senv (updEnvS env k v) s
  | StmtS.ssallS k s =>
      forall u, u ∈ sbox -> denoteStmtBoxS box sbox (updSenvS senv k u) env s

def checkStmtBoxS (box : List Int) (sbox : List (Int -> Bool))
    (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) : StmtS -> Bool
  | StmtS.base p => checkPdS box senv env p
  | StmtS.sallS k s =>
      box.all (fun v => checkStmtBoxS box sbox senv (updEnvS env k v) s)
  | StmtS.ssallS k s =>
      sbox.all (fun u => checkStmtBoxS box sbox (updSenvS senv k u) env s)

/-- SOUNDNESS of the set-binder sweep.  It goes through -- so the tower is
NOT blocked by proof obligations.  What it is relative to is `sbox`. -/
theorem checkStmtBoxS_sound (box : List Int) (sbox : List (Int -> Bool)) :
    (s : StmtS) -> (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) -> (env : Nat -> Int) ->
      checkStmtBoxS box sbox senv env s = true ->
        denoteStmtBoxS box sbox senv env s
  | StmtS.base p, senv, env, h => checkPdS_sound box senv env p h
  | StmtS.sallS k s, senv, env, h => by
      simp only [checkStmtBoxS, List.all_eq_true] at h
      intro v hv
      exact checkStmtBoxS_sound box sbox s senv (updEnvS env k v) (h v hv)
  | StmtS.ssallS k s, senv, env, h => by
      simp only [checkStmtBoxS, List.all_eq_true] at h
      intro u hu
      exact checkStmtBoxS_sound box sbox s (updSenvS senv k u) env (h u hu)

/-- For the sweep's verdict to mean what the emitted `forall U : Set Int`
says, `sbox` must be EVERY subset of the box.  This builds it. -/
def subsetsOfS : List Int -> List (Int -> Bool)
  | [] => [fun _ => false]
  | x :: xs =>
      (subsetsOfS xs) ++
        (subsetsOfS xs).map (fun u => fun y => if y = x then true else u y)

/-- THE MEASUREMENT, as a theorem instead of a paragraph: one set binder's
box-relativized domain is 2 ^ |box|.  At the committed Int box (2*8+1 = 17
values) that is 131072 set assignments for ONE set variable; the lead
subject needs two, beside an ordinary Int binder. -/
theorem subsetsOfS_length :
    (b : List Int) -> (subsetsOfS b).length = 2 ^ b.length
  | [] => rfl
  | x :: xs => by
      simp [subsetsOfS, List.length_append, List.length_map,
        subsetsOfS_length xs, Nat.pow_succ, Nat.mul_two]

/-- And the sweep over that domain is what a set binder COSTS: the checker
folds `sbox` at every set binder, so a statement with `n` set binders costs
`(2 ^ |box|) ^ n` leaf checks.  Stated for the two-binder shape the lead
subject actually has. -/
theorem ssall_two_binder_cost (box : List Int) (k1 k2 : Nat) (p : PdS)
    (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) :
    checkStmtBoxS box (subsetsOfS box) senv env
        (StmtS.ssallS k1 (StmtS.ssallS k2 (StmtS.base p)))
      = (subsetsOfS box).all (fun u1 =>
          (subsetsOfS box).all (fun u2 =>
            checkPdS box (updSenvS (updSenvS senv k1 u1) k2 u2) env p)) := rfl

The unmet requirement it leaves is that a free set variable is also a BINDER, and the certified pipeline decides a binder by SWEEPING its box-relativized domain.  r2's text is carried forward VERBATIM and this round adds exactly that one layer, so a regression is attributable: the box-relativized pred checker and its soundness lemma, the statement layer with BOTH binder kinds (ssallS is the set binder), the sweep, its soundness theorem, the powerset construction the sweep's domain must be, and the cardinality theorem subsetsOfS_length : (subsetsOfS b).length = 2 ^ b.length. honesty: A verdict row is lane evidence about ELABORATION, never a certificate and never a fidelity verdict. sorryAx in the audited axiom set is never a pass -- a candidate that merely elaborates with a hole is a well-formed hole, not a proof -- and audit silence fails CLOSED. This channel iterates at a SESSION BOUNDARY per ride, one round-trip per push and not per minute; it is the slow second route to tower-class work when tools/lean_env_probe.py reads lean-absent, never a replacement for a local toolchain and never a softening of PLAN_FRAGMENT 3.1 rule 3, whose lane verdict remains final.
